summary: path item extra in the generated document; 1 extra

answer.why_different: The generated document places a reusable `components` block at the `paths` level, making it a different address and an invalid Paths Object member. `PatchItem` itself is a specification-defined data type, but it is declared in the wrong location.
answer.spec_3gpp: The specification defines `PatchItem` as a data type and states that it specifies a patch item of a patch document, but the supplied specification evidence does not support placing it under `paths`.
answer.openapi: The OpenAPI reference says that the Paths Object holds relative endpoint paths, whose field names must begin with `/`; `components` is therefore not a valid member of `paths`. Reusable component definitions belong in the document’s components structure, not as a path entry.
answer.clearer_why: Although the generated side exposes a potentially useful `PatchItem` schema, placing it under `paths` makes the document invalid and presents it as an endpoint-related path item. The official side avoids this invalid extra path entry.

differences.reason: This is a wrong address: `components` was added inside `paths`. OpenAPI requires Paths Object field names to represent paths beginning with `/` (O6), while the specification only establishes `PatchItem` as a data type (S15), not as a path.

evidence.title: Relative References in URLs
evidence.text:
### Relative References in URLs  
Unless specified otherwise, all properties that are URLs MAY be relative references as defined by [RFC3986](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986#section-4.2).
Relative references are resolved using the URLs defined in the [`Server Object`](#server-object) as a Base URI.  
Relative references used in `$ref` are processed as per [JSON Reference](https://tools.ietf.org/html/draft-pbryan-zyp-json-ref-03), using the URL of the current document as the base URI. See also the [Reference Object](#reference-object).

#### Paths Object  
Holds the relative paths to the individual endpoints and their operations.
The path is appended to the URL from the [`Server Object`](#server-object) in order to construct the full URL.  The Paths MAY be empty, due to [ACL constraints](#security-filtering).
